name: colWeightedMeans
title: Calculates the weighted means for each row (column) in a matrix

origin.description: Calculates the weighted means for each row (column) in a matrix.
origin.usage:
colWeightedMeans(x, w = NULL, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, na.rm = FALSE,
  ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A numeric vector of length K (N).

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: The implementations of these methods are optimized for both speed and memory. If no weights are given, the corresponding rowMeans()/colMeans() is used.
origin.value: Returns a numeric vector of length N (K).
origin.example:
x <- matrix(1:12, nrow = 3, ncol = 4)
w <- c(1, 0, 1)
colWeightedMeans(x, w = w)

translation.description: Calculates the weighted mean of each column.
translation.usage:
colWeightedMeans(x, w=None, rows=None, cols=None, na_rm=False,
                use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d numeric, integer, or logical array. Axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, in printed order. A vector is rejected; this function has no dim argument. An int32 value of -2147483648 is R's integer NA.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: One numeric weight per row, checked against the full matrix before rows is applied. None uses an ordinary mean. A non-missing negative weight is an error. A missing weight stays in the product.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. Zero is dropped. A negative index drops that row, and a negative past the end is ignored. A numeric missing value inserts a missing row. Logical values, including a logical missing value, are recycled to the number of rows. The same index is applied to w.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts, with the same rules as rows.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values in x are excluded, but only through the path in the R file. This is na.rm. True or False only.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument useNames. The result is always a plain float64 vector, with no names attached.

translation.details: The formula is the one in R/rowWeightedMeans.R for columns. It does not call weightedMean. Zero weights are removed before missing values are read when fewer weights remain than the original number of rows. If a repeated subscript keeps at least that many weights, a zero stays and a missing value times zero stays missing. When na_rm is true and x has a missing value, a missing weight is omitted from the denominator and left in the product unless that cell of x is missing too. When na_rm is true and x has no missing value, the weights are scaled by their sum, so a missing weight makes every column missing.
translation.value: A float64 vector of length equal to the number of selected columns.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowweightedmeans import colWeightedMeans

x = np.array([[1, 4, 7, 10], [2, 5, 8, 11], [3, 6, 9, 12]], dtype=float)
colWeightedMeans(x, w=np.array([1.0, 0.0, 1.0]))
